For each x = (xij )i∈[n],j∈[k] ∈ {0, 1} , we define f ⊗n (x) to be the vector obtained by applying f to (xi1 , . . . , xik ), in place for each i ∈ [n] (see Definition 13).
context: We further extend this definition to what we call block-rigid functions (see Definition 11). nk For this, we’ll consider vectors x ∈ {0, 1} , which are thought of as composed of k blocks, nk nk each of size n. We say that a function f : {0, 1} → {0, 1} is not an (r, s)-block-rigid nk function, if there exists a subset X ⊆ {0, 1} of size at least 2nk−r , such that over X, each output block of f can be written as a function of some s input blocks. We conjecture that it is possible to obtain large block-rigid functions, using smaller rigid k k nk functions. For a function f : {0, 1} → {0, 1} , we define the function f ⊗n : {0, 1} → nk nk {0, 1} as follows. For each x = (xij )i∈[n],j∈[k] ∈ {0, 1} , we define f ⊗n (x) to be the vector obtained by applying f to (xi1 , . . . , xik ), in place for each i ∈ [n] (see Definition 13). I Conjecture 1. There exists a universal constant c > 0 such that the following is true. Let k k nk nk f : {0, 1} → {0, 1} be an (r, s)-rigid function, and n ∈ N.
